title: San Diego Rebate Guide 2026: SDG&E and Community Power
desc: Every home energy program for San Diego, Chula Vista and Escondido in 2026: SDG&E's coupons, Community Power battery and device rewards, and free upgrades for some households.
h1: San Diego Rebate Guide 2026: SDG&E and Community Power
lead: One utility delivers your power and, in most of San Diego County, another supplies it. This guide lists what each offers, read from their own pages on October 2, 2026. The older version of this guide called the battery program SGIP and gave no amounts.
sections: Batteries (SDCP): $250 to $500 per kWh, plus $0.10 per kWh for weekday evening discharge. Smart devices (SDCP): $50 per thermostat or heat pump water heater, up to three of each, plus yearly payments. EV charging (SDCP): $50 plus $5 a month. No-cost upgrades: for income-qualified owners and renters in identified communities. SDG&E coupons: $75 thermostat, $500 heat pump water heater replacing electric, but SDG&E says the retail offerings have ended. Heat pump HVAC: no open utility rebate that we found.
If you are in San Diego or Chula Vista

You are an SDCP customer. The battery rebate is for single-family homes with solar, and the battery must charge from the solar panels. The device program is a pilot that pays you for enrolling a thermostat or water heater you already own. Details: San Diego and Chula Vista.
Escondido buys from SDG&E, so the SDCP programs do not apply. Solar permits are streamlined through SolarAPP+. See Escondido.
The federal 25C and 25D credits ended after December 31, 2025. TECH Clean California and the federal HEEHRA program are fully reserved for single-family homes and take new requests on hold only.
faq: What does SDG&E pay for a heat pump?
We found no open SDG&E rebate for one.
Is there a battery incentive in San Diego?
Yes, from San Diego Community Power: $250 to $500 per kWh.
Possibly. The Equitable Building Decarbonization program offers no-cost upgrades to income-qualified households in identified communities.
